title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 157
paragraphs: In the manner described, then, Gelon had become a powerful tyrant. At this time, when the Greek envoys arrived at Syracuse, they came to confer with him and said: “The Lacedaemonians and their allies have sent us to get you to join them against the barbarian. We assume you know well of the man who is about to invade Greece — that a Persian is planning to bridge the Hellespont and lead an expedition against Greece, bringing with him out of Asia all the armies of the East, under the pretext of marching on Athens, but in fact intending to bring all of Greece under his power. You, seeing that you have risen to great power and have no small portion of Greece as your share, being ruler of Sicily, come to the aid of those striving to free Greece, and help to set her free. For if all Greece is gathered into one, it forms a great body, and we are a match for those coming against us. But if some of us go over to the enemy and others refuse to help, so that the sound part of Greece is only a small part, then at once there is a danger that all Greece may fall to ruin. Do not imagine that if the Persian defeats us in battle he will not also come against you — guard against this beforehand. In coming to our aid you are helping yourself. A thing planned wisely generally turns out well in the end.”
